claim: Is ADP/ATP specificity created outside or inside the nucleotide site?
finding: Crystal structures of the beta nucleotide-binding domain and of K46bE, K114bD, V113bL, L227bF and K46bE/K114bD show specificity arises from hydrogen bonds between adenine and Gln20b, Gly111b, Val113b; mutants have similar conformations; only Mg-ADP complexes obtained
context: Blastocystis hominis SCS beta subunit ATP-grasp domain, isolated from the alpha subunit
confidence: high for the bound state; no guanine-nucleotide complex and no alpha/beta structure

stance: supports entrance (as argued by the authors); qualifies on re-analysis
claim: Do charged residues outside the site control which nucleotide is used?
finding: WT: ATP Km 145+/-47 uM, kcat 0.0139+/-0.002 s-1, GTP ND. ED: ATP Km 230+/-34, kcat 0.0176; GTP Km 143+/-17, kcat 0.0195. LF: ATP Km 265+/-50, GTP ND. ED+LF: ATP ND to 1 mM; GTP Km 82+/-12, kcat 0.0078
context: refolded recombinant Blastocystis SCS alpha+beta, coupled assay
confidence: medium; refolded-from-inclusion-body enzyme, very low kcat (0.014 s-1), all WT GTP entries ND so no Km/kcat decomposition possible

evidence_type: direct assay + homology model, docking, MD
claim: Blastocystis SCS is ATP-specific despite a GTP-like binding site
finding: Enzyme is ATP-specific and localises to the mitochondrion-like organelle; modelling attributes GTP rejection to Lys42/Lys110 outside the cavity
context: Blastocystis sp., organelle localisation plus recombinant enzyme assay
confidence: medium; the structural part is a homology model with no experimental structure available at the time

claim: Can a charge change at residues 46 and 114 discriminate adenine from guanine at the mouth?
finding: Adenine 87% buried; open solid angle 4.0% at probe 2.0 A and zero at 2.4 A; mouth potential +0.87 kT/e (WT) vs +0.21 kT/e (ED), a base-blind 1.17 kcal/mol for any NTP; base-dipole term 0.036 kT aligned, 0.001 kT averaged, 55x smaller; Lys46 NZ and Lys114 NZ are 11.6 and 13.6 A off the channel axis
context: isolated beta ATP-grasp domain crystal structures, continuum solvent
confidence: medium; continuum monopole/dipole estimate, ignores desolvation and the missing alpha subunit

citation: PDB 2FP4 (pig GTP-specific SCS + GTP) vs 6NO0, this analysis
claim: Can Gln20b discriminate the two bases on hydrogen-bonding grounds?
finding: Gln20b occurs in both enzymes and contacts both bases at 2.6 A, but with inverted amide polarity (OE1...adenine N6 2.55 A vs NE2...guanine O6 2.58 A); backbone N and CA displaced 3.19 and 3.02 A; linker backbone reads the opposite base edge in each
context: pig GTP-specific SCS holoenzyme vs Blastocystis isolated beta domain
confidence: high for the measured distances; equivalence assigned by ligand superposition, not by sequence alignment

citation: PDB 3UFX (Thermus aquaticus SCS + GDP), this analysis
claim: Is a glutamine at the Gln20 position required for guanine use?
finding: No glutamine near the base; the only polar base contacts are backbone, Val94 O to N1 3.22 A and Val94 N to O6 3.19 A
context: Thermus aquaticus SCS, the enzyme that prefers GDP/GTP while carrying a basic residue at the first gatekeeper position

claim: What is the largest base discrimination a charged mouth can produce at this geometry?
finding: Base-blind charge term exceeds the base-specific dipole term by 5.8x (worst) to 103x (best), median 24x; the dipole term never reaches 1 kT, maximum 0.358 kT = 1.43-fold selectivity at perfect alignment, against complete exclusion observed
context: dielectric 78.5 and 40; ionic strength 0, 50, 150, 300 mM; 2-12 A along the path; full field vector
confidence: medium-high for the bound; continuum model, formal charges on tip atoms only

evidence_type: structural (channel and SASA with and without the alpha subunit)
claim: Does the missing alpha subunit invalidate channel geometry computed on the isolated beta domain?
finding: Nearest alpha atom to GTP 11.92 A, zero alpha atoms within 15 A of the base, identical open solid angle (8.75% at 1.4 A, 0.92% at 2.0 A, 0% at 2.4 A) and burial (GTP 73.6%, guanine 87.4%) with and without alpha; exit path stays 20.1-22.0 A from alpha
context: pig GTP-specific SCS with Mg-GTP, compared with Blastocystis 6NO0
confidence: high for the measurement; assumes the Blastocystis beta domain packs like the pig beta subunit

evidence_type: structural comparison, pocket composition by purine-ring superposition
claim: What else in the pocket differs from a GTP-specific enzyme?
finding: 5 of 10 base-lining positions differ (Gly111/Glu107, Val113/Leu109, Val48/Ala108, Cys110/Val44, Leu227/Phe219); V113bL and L227bF install the exact pig residues; Lys46 and Lys114 lie 7.44 and 5.78 A from the base, outside the 2.55-4.86 A lining shell
context: Blastocystis beta nucleotide-binding domain against pig GTP-specific beta subunit, ring RMSD 0.040 A
confidence: High for the distances. Equivalence from two superposition methods that agree everywhere except Leu227 (Phe219 against Asp220)

claim: Where does a real GTP-specific enzyme carry its extra negative charge?
finding: Pig is 2 charge units more negative at every radius 8-15 A around the base (-2 against 0 at 12 A); K46bE reproduces pig Glu42 but K114bD installs an aspartate where pig has Ser112
context: Same superposed frame, 173-pair global CA check RMSD 2.51 A
confidence: Medium-high. Formal charges only, no pKa calculation, single GTP-specific exemplar
